name: North Dakota

ttd.rateText: Weekly benefit equal to 66 2/3% of the gross average weekly wage, subject to a minimum of 60% and a maximum of 125% of the state average weekly wage (N.D.C.C. § 65-05-09(1)); WSI states the weekly benefit also cannot exceed net wages after taxes. A dependency allowance of $15 per week per child is added (§ 65-05-08(10)).
ttd.minText: Minimum is 60% of the SAWW unless that exceeds the employee's net wages (gross wages minus federal income tax and social security), in which case net wages are paid (WSI benefit levels notes).
ttd.periodLabel: disability on or after July 1, 2026 (rates in effect on the date of first disability apply); SAWW $1,291

waiting.text: Benefits may not be paid for disability lasting less than five consecutive calendar days (N.D.C.C. § 65-05-08). Stored as a 4-day threshold: a disability of five days or more is paid from the first day, since the statute sets no separate unpaid waiting period once the threshold is met.

ttdDuration.text: No fixed week limit on temporary total disability; benefits continue during the disability, but an employee who retires or begins receiving social security retirement benefits is presumed retired from the labor market and disability benefits end (N.D.C.C. § 65-05-09.3). Temporary partial disability is limited to 5 years (WSI).

ppd.text: Permanent partial impairment (PPI) awards are lump sums equal to 35% of the state average weekly wage on the date of the impairment evaluation, rounded to the next highest dollar, multiplied by a statutory multiplier tied to the impairment percentage (N.D.C.C. § 65-05-12.2). The PPI rate is $452 for evaluations from July 1, 2026.

facts.text: North Dakota is a monopolistic state fund: WSI describes itself as the sole provider and administrator of the workers' compensation system in North Dakota.
Since August 1, 2009, the maximum weekly benefit equals 125% of the state average weekly wage (before that, 110%); rates are reset every July 1.
Disability benefits are reduced by one-half of any Social Security disability benefit received (N.D.C.C. § 65-05-09.1).
An employer may not require an injured employee to use sick leave or paid time off before or instead of receiving disability benefits (N.D.C.C. § 65-05-08).
Benefits are not paid for wage loss related to the use or presence of medical marijuana (N.D.C.C. § 65-05-08(12)).

uncertain: The net-wage ceiling on the weekly benefit is stated by WSI (wage-loss benefits page and benefit-levels notes); the exact statutory subsection was not located in § 65-05-09 text extracted.
Temporary partial disability 5-year limit taken from the WSI wage-loss benefits page (https://www.workforcesafety.com/employees/benefits-services/wage-loss-benefits).

Waiting period encoded as days 4 / retroactiveAfterDays 4 (paid in full once disability reaches 5 days); § 65-05-08 does not say expressly that the first days are paid once the 5-day threshold is met.
